mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate increases by >0.5pp in a month but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a weakening housing market, which is a key component of consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST both decline in the same month but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 0.5% month-over-month), manufacturing output expansion boosts corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% MoM but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (measured by retail sales, RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average indicates robust demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS remains above its 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals rising inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3pp in a month but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a labor market contraction with reduced workforce participation, which lowers consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS and UNRATE both decline in the same month but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL < 2.0% year-over-year), a decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary easing, which boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% YoY and FEDFUNDS declines but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.
